catalog_quote: Une étude morphotonologique s'avère bien entendu indispensable . Je n'ai pas trouvé d'oppositions permettant de poser l'existence de trois tons . Par contre, l'abaissement du ton haut est fréquent . Il semble systématique dans les verbes bi- ou trisyllabiques à la forme inaccomplie, lorsque les deux dernières syllabes sont de tons hauts . Le dernier est alors abaissé et s'oppose au ton bas de l'accompli lorsque la forme est par ailleurs similaire . nè wéésí [ nè wé : s1 ] “ je cherche " nè wéésì [ nè wé : sì ] “ j'ai cherché " nè símésí [ nè símési ] " je parle " [ nè símésì ] " j'ai parlé " ... [Pali 2011, thesis abstract:] Sur le plan tonal, trois niveaux se distinguent : haut, moyen et bas.

new_statements.translation: ... tone. A morphotonological study is of course indispensable. I have found no oppositions that would allow positing the existence of three tones. On the other hand, lowering (downstep) of the high tone is frequent. It seems systematic in bi- or trisyllabic verbs in the imperfective form, when the last two syllables are high-toned: the last one is then lowered and contrasts with the low tone of the perfective ... [Pali 2011 abstract:] On the tonal level, three levels are distinguished: high, mid and low.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Miyobe is described as a tone language (Rongier 1996: two level tones H/L with frequent, grammatically conditioned downstep of H; Pali 2011: three levels H/M/L). No opened or snippet-visible source says anything about word stress or accent; snippet searches for 'accent', 'accentuation', 'intensité', 'accent tonique' inside Rongier 1996 and Person 1955 returned nothing.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any accessible text.
new_statements.exceptions: The two sources disagree on the number of tone levels (Rongier: no evidence for a third tone, but systematic downstep; Pali: three levels H, M, L) — Pali's 'mid' may correspond to Rongier's downstepped high, but this cannot be checked without the full texts.
new_statements.domain_note: Rongier's downstep remark concerns bi-/trisyllabic verb forms (imperfective vs perfective); Pali's statement is a thesis-abstract summary of the tonal system of the language, domain unspecified. The quoted text comes from Google Books snippets and an official thesis abstract, not from a page opened by me; no page locator is available.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to the same language miyo1238 under different names: mɔyɔbɛ/moyobe (Rongier 1996), miyobé (Pali 2011), biyobè/uyóbè/Soruba (Person 1955), Sol(l)a (exonym, Güldemann 2018). Rongier's snippet mentions correcting an earlier 'solla' wordlist whose terms were 'souvent si éloignés de la réalité'. No dialect is specified in any accessible text; Ceccaldi 1979 (Gallica) cites Person for a 'Minatyire' dialect 'très proche du miyobe'.
